project: topweb — PHP REST API + Web Frontend
summary: Restructured a single-version PHP REST API into a dual-version (V1 + V2) architecture running in parallel, deployed to production server, integrated the web frontend login with the V2 Bearer token system, created test users (admin, admin1, mojarra) with password 1234, created a permission-less test user (sinpermisos / INACTIVE), and generated a full Postman collection covering all V1+V2 endpoints with Bearer-token automation.

work_done.title: Shared Core — Router & Entry Point
work_done.description: Refactored Router.php and rewrote index.php to support dual-version dispatch without Docker.

changes.key_change: dispatch() now returns true (route matched) or false (no match) instead of echoing a 404 directly. Allows v1 and v2 routers to chain in index.php.

changes.logic: Creates one Router('v1') and one Router('v2'), registers their routes separately, then runs: if (!routerV1->dispatch() && !routerV2->dispatch()) -> 404. CORS preflight (OPTIONS) handled at the top.

work_done.title: Web Frontend — V2 Token Integration
work_done.description: Integrated the web frontend (login.php, logout.php, crud.php) with the V2 Bearer token system. The web session now also holds an API token obtained at login and revoked at logout.

changes.what_changed: After a successful web session auth (usuarios table), login.php now also calls POST /api/v2/login via file_get_contents. The Bearer token and expiry are stored in $_SESSION['api_token'] and $_SESSION['api_expires_at']. The API username is derived from the email prefix (admin@miapp.local -> admin). Token failure is non-blocking — web session continues even if API token is unavailable.

Before destroying the PHP session, logout.php now calls POST /api/v2/logout with the stored Bearer token to revoke it server-side. If no token exists or revocation fails, the session is still destroyed cleanly.

Added a token status badge below the header. When a V2 token is active, shows the truncated token value and expiry time (green badge). When unavailable, shows a warning (red badge). No existing CRUD logic was modified.

auth_flow: 1. User submits email + password on login.php
2. Web auth: query usuarios table, verify bcrypt hash -> set $_SESSION['usuario_id'] + nombre
3. API auth: POST /api/v2/login with {username: email_prefix, password} -> store $_SESSION['api_token'] + api_expires_at
4. crud.php shows token badge and uses session for all page-level auth
5. logout.php: POST /api/v2/logout (revokes token) -> session_destroy() -> redirect to login.php

design_decisions: Class prefix strategy (V1_, V2_) instead of PHP namespaces — compatible with PHP 5-style codebase.
Router.dispatch() returns bool so two routers chain cleanly in a single if-statement without double output.
V2 auth uses constant-time password_verify with a dummy hash when user not found — prevents username enumeration via timing attack.
V1 completely untouched in behavior — origin/main logic read from git and reproduced exactly.
api_tokens uses ON DELETE CASCADE — deleting an api_user auto-cleans their tokens.
login.php API token failure is non-blocking — web session works even if api_users has no matching account.
API username derived from email prefix (admin@miapp.local -> admin) — zero extra form fields needed.
database.php is patched automatically by deploy script per environment — developer never edits it manually.
No Docker used on server — raw Apache/PHP/MySQL shared hosting.
constraints_respected: V1 logic completely untouched — verified against git origin/main
V2 fully isolated — separate models, resources, and auth filter
Single entry point (api/public/index.php) handles both versions

All files PHP-syntax-checked before every deployment
Existing production data (12 products) preserved — INSERT IGNORE used in SQL migration
Test users created via PHP script on server to avoid bcrypt dollar-sign shell interpolation issues.
